evidence.description: The actor-isolated method suspends during the network request, allowing another invocation to start before this invocation resumes.
Returned values and timestamps are assigned without checking whether they are older than the current state.

candidates.explanation: Actor isolation prevents simultaneous state access but does not preserve ordering across the network await. If overlapping requests complete out of order, an older response can overwrite statistics already updated by a newer response. Even the statistics with explicit last-updated timestamps can regress because those timestamps are assigned without comparison.
candidates.title: Overlapping fetches can overwrite newer statistics

evidence.description: The response accompanying the downloaded data is discarded, and the body is decoded and applied without any HTTP status validation.

candidates.explanation: URLSession does not throw solely because an HTTP response has an unsuccessful status. Consequently, this method treats an error response as statistics data: it can report only a decoding error rather than the HTTP failure, or even update state if the unsuccessful response body matches the expected schema.
candidates.title: HTTP response status is ignored
